_note: Reviewed policy statements for Minnesota state-legislature quizzes. Each is a statement of a real, currently contested MN policy approach — the bias-audit pipeline (generate variants -> blind score -> select) produces the neutral question text; these statements are never shown to voters. One question per topic per race (the generator enforces this; see the 2026-09 dedupe).

topics.statement: Create a public option allowing any Minnesotan to buy into MinnesotaCare, the state's subsidized health insurance program.
Create a new, higher state income tax tier on annual income above one million dollars.
Fully exempt all Social Security benefits from Minnesota state income tax, regardless of the recipient's income.
Create education savings accounts or vouchers that let families use state per-pupil funding toward private school tuition.
Require cities to allow duplexes and small multifamily housing on lots currently zoned exclusively for single-family homes.
Keep and enforce Minnesota's extreme risk protection order (red flag) law, which lets courts temporarily remove firearms from people found to be a danger to themselves or others.
Keep Minnesota's requirement that electric utilities deliver 100 percent carbon-free electricity by 2040.
Keep Minnesota's paid family and medical leave program, funded by a payroll tax split between employers and workers, which began paying benefits in 2026.
Increase mandatory minimum prison sentences for repeat violent offenders.
Keep Minnesota's law allowing residents to obtain a driver's license regardless of immigration status.
Keep the metro-area sales tax dedicated to funding public transit expansion and operations.
Allow cities and counties to prohibit licensed cannabis retail businesses within their borders.
